source.title: Intricacies of Feature Geometry in Large Language Models

record.tranche_reason: The post examines feature geometry in LLMs, but it does not test or use the claim about superposition, capacity-driven polysemanticity, SAE features, or one-dimensional superposed features. Its own geometry findings concern concept vectors after whitening.
record.gate_note: The post reports qualitative geometry findings for emotion concepts, random nonsense concepts, and random unembeddings. These concern whitened concept-vector orthogonality and polytopes, not any listed claim version, so the rows are recorded with versions ["none"]. Results the post attributes to the original geometry papers are not recorded as its own findings.
record.test_reason: The post critiques Park et al.'s whitened 'causal inner product' geometry, covering orthogonality of hierarchical concepts and polytopes of categorical concepts in Gemma-2B. It never tests superposition, capacity-driven polysemanticity, SAE features or feature dimensionality. SAEs and non-linear features appear only in a related-works list. Its note that random high-dimensional vectors are nearly orthogonal (Johnson–Lindenstrauss) is background math about probe geometry, not a test of V1.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. More precisely, the authors say the orthogonality and polytope results of Park et al. are a 'trivial consequence of the whitening transformation and the high dimensionality'. They add that a transformation making opposite concepts orthogonal is unsuitable for studying models.
record.recipe_differences: The post says its emotion and nonsense ablations use the original geometry paper's code and hyperparameters, but this is different from the Toy Models of Superposition method and does not test superposition.

fits_no_version.finding: After whitening, emotion opposites (joy vs. sadness) and random nonsense categories in Gemma-2B show the same orthogonality as animal hierarchies. Random categories also form simplices.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Orthogonality and polytope structure under the whitened causal inner product arise for arbitrary or opposite concepts, so they do not show meaningful concept geometry.

fits_no_version.finding: Random, untrained unembedding matrices show the same orthogonality and animal-category polytopes after whitening.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Whitened concept-vector geometry does not emerge from training; it follows from whitening and high dimensionality.

record.problems: The post describes its empirical results qualitatively, without numerical geometry measures or uncertainty estimates in the text. The datasets and random-unembedding comparisons are described, but their plotted values are not provided here.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, sparsity sweep or feature-storage geometry.
All: no neuron-level polysemanticity or capacity allocation.
All: polysemantic neurons are not examined.
All: no measurement of features spread across neurons and no SAE recovery.
All: SAE features are mentioned only in related works.
All: non-linear features are mentioned only as a citation.

record.verdict_notes: The relation is changed from 'discusses' to 'cites_only': superposition is not discussed, and SAEs appear only in related works. All rows correctly carry versions ['none']. Rows are qualitative descriptions of figures with no numeric values, which is acceptable here since none bears on a version.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model feature overlap, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity or allocates dedicated dimensions to important features.
Whether polysemantic neurons can arise without capacity pressure.
Whether real models spread features across neurons or contain sparse features recoverable by an SAE.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, canonical units of model representation.
Whether superposed features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.
